target_customer: Pokemon card collectors, investors and sellers, especially graded and sealed products
problem: Collectible pricing is opaque and scattered across auction houses and forums. Misprint combines pricing analytics with a bid and ask marketplace.

founders.name: Eva Herget
education: University of Chicago, economics and East Asian languages and civilizations
previous_startups: Full time Pokemon card selling business, reported over $500k ARR within three months
founders.background_notes: Runs the YouTube channel Eva's Binder per the company site.

founders.name: Jon Jenkins
founders.background_notes: Surname from a standout.work listing; the company site gives only Jon. Described as best friend of Eva since Exeter.

competitors.name: TCGplayer
competitors.what: Main marketplace and price reference for Pokemon cards

competitors.name: Collectr
competitors.what: Free multi game collection and price tracking app

competitors.name: Whatnot
competitors.what: Live selling platform used for sealed product and cards

technical_complexity.rationale: A live order book marketplace plus ML pricing models needs data infrastructure, trading engine logic and fraud handling, moderate for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: A bid and ask book needs liquidity on both sides, but TCGplayer, eBay and Whatnot already hold the buyers and sellers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already pricing and selling cards; no copy of the order book model found.

market_need_then: Collectors complain of opaque prices; the founder reports $500k ARR from her own card selling in three months (company claim). Trading card demand was rising per the company pitch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Finance flavored positioning: Robinhood, but make it Pokemon cards

branding.brand_signature: Launch line: Robinhood, but make it Pokemon cards
branding.community_and_virality: Founder's YouTube channel Eva's Binder and a company claim of a 4.9 rating from over 13,000 reviews; no independent brand press found.

brand_strength.rationale: A real word with a collector flavor on an exact .com plus a clear launch line and a founder with a collecting audience, but no independent press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Misprint is an active four person YC Winter 2025 company whose CEO built a card selling business before founding it, a strong domain fit. No funding amounts, exit or shutdown are public. It competes against TCGplayer, eBay and Whatnot, so liquidity is the central risk and the outcome is still open.
notes: A zerogtalent listing marks Seed raised with no amount or investors, so no round is recorded. The company about page returned HTTP 429. Competitor sources are 2026 era guides describing the 2025 landscape; no dated launch coverage near 2025-01 was found.
